passage: In the village near Sangli, Akash sat on the low stool in the yard each evening, pressing coconut oil into Jahnavi's tired hands while the light went orange. Jahnavi, Akash's mother, had walked eight kilometres to sell vegetables so Akash could finish school, and Akash remembered the blisters. Now the roles had turned. Gratitude rose in Akash's chest, warm and heavy, and it did not feel like a debt. It felt like being allowed to do something loving. Jahnavi hummed an old film song. Akash sang the second line. Later, at the well, a cousin offered to sit with Jahnavi for an hour on Thursdays. "Take it," the cousin said. "You need your walk too." Akash nodded, surprised at how easy it was to say yes.

qa.q: What did Akash do each evening in the yard?
qa.a: Akash sat on the low stool and pressed coconut oil into Jahnavi's hands.

qa.q: What did Akash feel while remembering what Jahnavi gave?
qa.a: Warm and heavy gratitude that did not feel like a debt but like being allowed to do something loving.

qa.q: Why is it wise for Akash to accept the cousin's offer?
qa.a: Caring with patience and warmth lasts longer if Akash also looks after Akash's own health, and an hour off on Thursdays for a walk makes that possible.

qa.q: How might Jahnavi feel about Akash's evening care?
qa.a: Probably comforted and proud, since Jahnavi hums an old film song and Akash sings the next line, which suggests the moment is warm for both.

grounding: Shows a parent needing care, the protagonist remembering what the parent gave and feeling deep gratitude, caring with patience and warmth and also looking after their own health.

Kiran: Papa slept after lunch finally. Took him 40 mins to finish the khichdi
Kishore: you ok didi?
Kiran: tired. But feeding him today, I remembered how he used to feed us rice with his hands when we had fever
Kiran: he'd make little balls and call them laddoos
Kishore: omg the fake laddoos 😄 I forgot
Kiran: I kept thinking, he never once rushed us
Kiran: so I'm trying not to rush him either 🙂
Kishore: you're amazing. But when did you last sleep 7 hours
Kiran: …
Kishore: exactly. I'm coming Saturday. You go for your walk and see your own doctor about that back
Kiran: ok ok. booked for Monday
Kishore: good. Papa gave us everything, but he wouldn't want you breaking yourself for it
Kiran: I know. I'm just so grateful I get to do this ❤️

qa.q: How long did it take Papa to finish the khichdi?
What was Kiran feeling while feeding Papa?
qa.a: Kiran felt deeply grateful and tender, remembering how Papa fed them patiently when they were ill.

qa.q: What advice did Kishore give, and why was it wise?
qa.a: He told Kiran to walk and see a doctor about the back, because caring well also means protecting your own health.

qa.q: How might Kishore feel reading his sister's messages?
qa.a: Kishore feels touched by the memory and worried about how tired she is 🥺

grounding: A chat shows a young woman caring for her ageing father with patience and deep gratitude, reminded by her brother to look after her own health too.

passage:
In Pranav's village near Dharwad, the power went off every afternoon, so he fanned his mother by hand while she napped. Since her stroke she could barely lift a spoon.

Sometimes, fanning her, he remembered the year of his board exams. She had walked four kilometres to the bus stand every morning with him, carrying his tiffin, and waited at the gate until he came out. He hadn't thanked her then. He was sixteen and embarrassed.

Now he combed her hair slowly, the way she used to comb his. When she spilled her tea, he wiped it and said, "No hurry, Avva."

His friend Tanvir came by one evening and found him asleep sitting up. "You look worse than her," he said. "Go and lie down. I'll sit with Avva. And show that back of yours at the health centre tomorrow."

Pranav slept three hours straight. The next morning he went to the health centre.

qa.q: How far did Pranav's mother walk with him each morning during his board exams?
qa.a: She walked four kilometres to the bus stand with him.

qa.q: What does Pranav's slow combing of his mother's hair suggest he feels?
qa.a: It suggests deep gratitude and tenderness, remembering all she did for him when he was young.

qa.q: What did Tanvir help Pranav see?
qa.a: That caring for Avva also means resting and seeing to his own health, so he can keep going.

qa.q: How does Tanvir see Pranav's situation?
qa.a: Tanvir is worried about his friend, noticing he looks worn out, and steps in so Pranav can rest.

grounding: The passage shows a young man caring for his frail mother with patience out of deep gratitude, and learning to look after his own health too.
